conviction_note: Eight small sourced items that roughly cancel: an AUM/futures tailwind to asset-based fees that is mostly computable and likely in the $880-889M revenue bar, against the risk that the same AUM rise pushes AUM-linked comp accruals and the expense guide up again (the line that cost -10% in July); p_up 50 on balanced evidence and mild put skew, abs_move 7.0 from the 6.5% event-implied move and a 5.7% median / 10.1% max reaction history.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $4.99 (Zacks) to $5.02-5.03 (Benzinga, TipRanks, TickerLeague; range $4.92-5.24, 8-12 analysts); revenue $880.3M (Zacks) to $883.8-889.4M. Two+ sources agree within ~1%. https://tickerleague.com/companies/MSCI/estimates ; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MSCI/earnings-forecasts . Company gives no revenue/EPS guidance; it guides FY2026 expenses: opex $1,535-1,575M, adj EBITDA expense $1,340-1,370M (raised $45M/$35M in July, at the high end) https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/MSCI/2607210634
positioning_check: Short interest ~1.2M shares (~1.6% of float), ~1.3 days to cover, falling, as of 2026-08-19 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/msci/summary); sweep cites 1.6-2.5% float, 1.3-3.2 DTC. Not a crowded short. Options: event-implied move 6.5%, 25d skew +2.21 vol pts (mild downside paid), put/call OI 2.93 on thin total OI 1,668. Stock is -13.1% from its 52w high, +0.05% over 20d, -1.54% over 5d, after a -10.1% reaction to the July print. Director Rajat Taneja bought $1.0M at $560 on 2026-09-02 (stock now $559).

findings.finding: Asset-based-fee tailwind: MSCI-linked ETF AUM ended Q2 at $2,818B against a Q2 average of $2,706B (Q2 ABF $233.1M at a 2.28bp period-end fee), and Q3 markets held that level (S&P 500 +2.3%, MSCI EAFE +0.9%, MSCI EM -0.2% for Q3 2026; global ETF assets $23.09T Jun -> $23.11T Jul -> $24.03T Aug per ETFGI; BlackRock iShares ~$135B Q3 inflows; ICE MSCI futures ADV +22% y/y in August), so Q3 average AUM is plausibly ~5-7% above Q2's average, implying ABF of roughly $240-248M (+$7-15M q/q) net of continued bp compression; that alone covers most of the ~$13-22M sequential revenue growth the $880-889M consensus embeds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 ABF grew 26.6% and the ABF run rate +25% to $948M, yet the stock fell -10.14% on 2026-07-21 on a small EPS miss and a raised expense guide; strong ABF has not protected this name when expenses/sales disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: AUM is computable from public index and ETF data and sell-side models it; if it were not in the bar, consensus revenue would sit near Q2's $867M rather than $880-889M. The residual edge is only whether the quarter-average uplift and futures volumes beat a model that assumed flat Q3 markets after a +15.6% Q2 appreciation.
findings.independence: Market data https://novelinvestor.com/2026-q3-returns/ (2026-10-07); ETFGI July report https://etfgi.com/node/28936 (2026-08-19); BlackRock Q3 https://www.blackrock.com/corporate/newsroom/media/press-releases/blackrock-reports-third-quarter-2026 (2026-10-14); ICE August MSCI ADV +22% https://s2.q4cdn.com/154085107/files/doc_news/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-August-2026-Statistics-2026.pdf . All proxies for the company's own AUM, not company numbers.

findings.finding: Expense-guide risk: in July MSCI raised FY2026 opex guidance by $45M to $1,535-1,575M and adj EBITDA expense by $35M, explicitly citing First Street (closed 2026-08-03, already in the guide) and higher incentive comp accruals from AUM growth above its prior flat-market assumption, and moved to the high end; AUM rose again in Q3, so a further nudge up or a 'high end' reiteration of the expense guide is plausible on the same line that drove the -10% July reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-21: raised expense guide plus ~1% EPS miss -> -10.14% (https://www.tikr.com/blog/msci-nyse-stock-tumbles-after-second-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-miss-wall-street-targets).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is still -13% from its high and the skew mildly favours puts. If a second raise were fully expected the bar EPS would have drifted down since July; it sits at $4.99-5.03, ~+1% above Q2's $4.94, implying the Street holds the guide roughly flat. Management also said it can flex investment spend, which caps the risk.
findings.independence: Shares the AUM driver with the ABF finding (higher AUM lifts both fees and comp accruals), so the two partly offset by construction. Q2 call transcript confirms the accrual mechanism: https://www.webull.com/news/15266275730072576

findings.finding: Sustainability & Climate drag: Q2 S&C revenue grew only 3.4% to $91.9M, cancellations (mainly Americas) rose ~40% y/y to $7.4M, and management guided S&C recurring net new sales to roughly zero to slightly negative for the next two quarters, i.e. Q3 and Q4 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: S&C cancellations were one of the analyst concerns on the July call that preceded the -10.14% day; S&C is ~11% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is inside what management guided. Only a print worse than 'slightly negative' would surprise; net of Index (59% of revenue, +17.5%) the segment cannot move the total much.

findings.finding: Counterparty demand read: FactSet (reported 2026-09-30 for the quarter to 2026-08-31, overlapping MSCI's Q3) grew organic ASV 7.0% to $2,568M with retention above 95% and growth across institutional buy-side, wealth and hedge funds, beating EPS ($4.52 vs ~$4.32), though its FY2027 guide was reported below expectations; MSCI itself flagged record hedge-fund run-rate growth (+19%) and a 'strong second-half pipeline, including some large potential deals'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscription sales were the other concern in July (Q2 sales felt short; Analytics organic run rate +7%); in Oct 2025 and Jan/Apr 2026 prints with solid run-rate growth the stock rose +8.6%, +5.7%, +5.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer read-through landing after MSCI last spoke; MSCI's bar barely moved after it. Weak transmission: FactSet's buyer overlap with MSCI Analytics is real but its FY27 guide was soft, so the read is mixed.
findings.independence: MSCI Q2 call on hedge funds and H2 pipeline: https://www.webull.com/news/15266275730072576 (company statement, priced since July).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction link; CEO buying preceded the +5.4% April print and the -10.1% July print alike.
